Odoo for NDT Inspection Companies: Complete Guide 2026

How Odoo's modular ERP framework becomes a purpose-built platform for NDT inspection company operations.

By Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III · July 24, 2026

Odoo for NDT inspection companies means using Odoo's open, modular ERP framework as the foundation for inspection-specific operations, report generation, technician certification tracking, calibration management, project scheduling, and invoicing, customized with NDT-specific modules rather than generic manufacturing or retail workflows. It gives inspection companies enterprise ERP capability without the cost or rigidity of legacy platforms like SAP.

Why Odoo Fits NDT Companies Better Than Legacy ERP

Most ERP platforms built for manufacturing or retail assume a bill-of-materials and inventory-driven business model that does not match how inspection companies actually operate. NDT companies sell certified labor and equipment time against a set of codes and standards, not manufactured units. Odoo's modular architecture, where you enable only the apps you need and extend them with custom modules, fits this reality far better than forcing an inspection workflow into a platform like SAP that was designed around discrete manufacturing. It also avoids the multi-year, high-cost implementation cycles that legacy platforms like IBM Maximo often require for a company the size of a typical regional NDT provider.

Odoo's Native Modules That Map to NDT Operations

Odoo ships with mature, well-tested modules that cover most of an inspection company's back office without custom development:

  • Project: work order scheduling, crew assignment, task tracking per job site
  • Inventory: equipment, consumables, and radiation source tracking with serial/lot numbers
  • Invoicing and Accounting: job costing tied to completed scope, multi-currency for international clients
  • Documents: version-controlled storage for procedures and quality manuals
  • CRM: managing client relationships and inspection contract renewals
  • Field Service: dispatching technicians and capturing job completion in the field

These modules alone give an inspection company a functional operational backbone. The gap is that none of them, by default, understand what an ASNT Level II certification is or when a UT gauge needs recalibration.

What Has to Be Custom-Built: NDT-Specific Layers

The value of Odoo for NDT companies comes from what gets added on top of the native modules. This includes method-specific inspection report templates (UT, RT, MT, PT, VT, ET, TOFD, Phased Array) mapped to relevant codes such as API 510, API 570, API 653, and ASME Section V, digital sign-off workflows enforcing SNT-TC-1A or ISO 9712 certification levels, and calibration tracking linked to ISO 17025-traceable standards. A properly configured Odoo-based NDT ERP builds these as first-class modules rather than workarounds, so the certification and calibration logic is enforced automatically instead of relying on manual checks.

Certification Tracking in Odoo

A certification tracking module built on Odoo's employee and HR framework extends technician records with method, level (I, II, III), issuing body, exam date, and expiration. Scheduling logic then cross-references this data before a technician can be assigned to a work order requiring that certification, and automated alerts flag renewals 60-90 days ahead of expiry. This turns a compliance requirement that many companies still track in a spreadsheet into an enforced system rule.

Calibration Management in Odoo

Built on Odoo's maintenance and equipment modules, a calibration management module tracks every instrument's calibration due date, the reference standard used, and the accredited lab that performed it. Reports generated through the system automatically pull the current calibration status of the instrument used, creating a permanent link between a specific reading and the equipment's calibration record at the time it was taken, exactly what an API or client audit will ask to see.

Field Reporting and Mobile Data Capture

Odoo's mobile-responsive interface and offline-capable apps extend naturally to field data capture, letting technicians complete method-specific report templates on a tablet at a tank farm or pipeline right-of-way with no connectivity, syncing automatically once back in range. Photos, defect maps, and thickness grids captured in the field flow directly into the report and the underlying project record, with no re-entry step.

Multi-Company and Multi-Crew Considerations

Odoo's native multi-company structure suits inspection groups operating across multiple regions or under separate legal entities, for example a US operation and an India-based operation under one parent company, while still consolidating reporting and financials at the group level. Crew scheduling logic can be configured to respect region-specific certification requirements, since ISO 9712 and SNT-TC-1A recognition varies by client and jurisdiction.

Migrating From Spreadsheets or Legacy Software to Odoo

Companies moving off spreadsheets or an aging standalone reporting tool typically migrate in phases: certification and calibration records first, since these carry the highest compliance risk if mismanaged, followed by active project and work order data, then historical report archives for audit continuity. A phased migration keeps the business running through the transition rather than requiring a hard cutover that risks losing operational continuity during a busy inspection season.

Odoo vs. SAP vs. Maximo for Inspection Companies

SAP and IBM Maximo are built for large enterprise asset owners managing thousands of assets across a facility, not for the inspection service providers who supply data into those systems. For a regional or mid-size NDT company, implementing SAP or Maximo internally is typically overkill on cost and complexity. Odoo, customized for NDT, delivers the connected operational capability a growing inspection company needs, while still exporting or integrating cleanly with a client's SAP or Maximo environment when required. This is the practical middle ground: enterprise-grade internal operations without enterprise-grade internal overhead. Frequently Asked Questions

Q1: Is Odoo good for small NDT inspection companies?

A: Yes. Odoo's modular pricing model, enabling only the apps a company needs, and its lower implementation overhead compared to SAP or Maximo make it accessible for small and mid-size inspection companies that still need enterprise-grade certification and calibration controls.

Q2: Does Odoo natively support NDT certification tracking?

A: Not out of the box. Native Odoo HR modules track basic employee data, but ASNT and ISO 9712-specific certification tracking, with method, level, and expiry logic tied to scheduling, requires a purpose-built module added on top of Odoo's framework.

Q3: Can Odoo handle multi-method NDT reporting?

A: Yes, when configured with method-specific report templates for UT, RT, MT, PT, VT, ET, TOFD, and Phased Array, each mapped to the relevant code such as API 510, 570, 653, or ASME Section V, Odoo can manage the full range of inspection methods within one system.

Q4: How does Odoo compare to IBM Maximo for NDT companies?

A: Maximo is built for enterprise asset owners managing large facility asset registers, not for inspection service providers. Odoo, customized for NDT operations, is a better operational fit for inspection companies while still integrating with a client's Maximo environment when needed.

Q5: How long does it take to migrate to an Odoo-based NDT ERP?

A: Timelines vary by company size, but a phased migration, starting with certification and calibration data, then active projects, then historical archives, typically allows a company to keep operating without a disruptive hard cutover.
